# My Thoughts On This Year's Farming

Aiyo, let me think about this. I've been doing this 50 years, so most of it I already know. But every year is a little different.

My 12 mu is split like I've always done it — 8 mu for the wheat and maize rotation, and 4 mu in cotton on the piece further from the house. I keep the cotton smaller now because picking is hard work. When my husband and I were younger we did more, but at our age 4 mu is enough. During picking season my daughter comes back to help, or I pay a neighbor woman 80-100 yuan a day for a few days.

## Wheat (8 mu)

My wheat went in the ground last October — I didn't plant this month, it's already growing. Now in April it's jointing, so I need to think about the spring topdress and the spring waterings. I used Jimai variety seed I bought at the agricultural supply store, same as last year. It did alright, about 450 kg/mu last harvest, not bad.

Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu and plowed it in. Now in spring I'll topdress urea — the extension guy said 10 kg urea per mu but I usually do about 12 kg because my field on the east side has poor soil. I already gave it the green-up water in March. I'll irrigate again at jointing (now), and once more at heading if it doesn't rain. Three times total this spring, each watering costs me maybe 30-35 yuan per mu in pumping fees. Expensive, but you have to.

Weeds I sprayed with herbicide back in late winter, one time, costs about 15 yuan/mu. I don't spray for insects unless I see them — my wheat hasn't had serious aphid trouble the last few years.

Harvest will be first week of June. I hire the combine, 50 yuan/mu.

## Summer Maize (8 mu)

Right after wheat comes off, I have maybe 5-6 days to get maize in. My son-in-law comes with the no-till planter, costs me 40 yuan/mu including seed placement. I use Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever the shop has that year. I don't plow — no time, and the straw mulch is fine.

Fertilizer: I drop compound (about 30 kg/mu of 15-15-15) at planting with the planter, then topdress urea around 12 kg/mu at the big-flare stage in late July. That's what works for me. Total N around 14 kg/mu. The soil here has decent phosphorus already from years of applying compound.

Irrigation for maize: usually 1-2 times if the summer rains are weak. Some years I don't irrigate at all because August rains cover it. I'll wait and see.

Pest spray for borer — one time, about 10 yuan/mu. Harvest end of September, combine again.

Last year maize gave me about 500 kg/mu, I'll aim for about the same.

## Cotton (4 mu)

Cotton I plant at the end of April, in about a week. I cover with plastic film to warm the soil — this is tradition here, everyone does it. Seed is Lu Mian variety, maybe 3 kg/mu. I already put down compound fertilizer (about 30 kg/mu) when I prepared the bed last week, and I'll topdress urea maybe twice — once at squaring and once at flowering, maybe 8 kg urea per mu each time.

Cotton needs more spraying — aphids, bollworm, sometimes red spider mite. I'll spray maybe 4-5 times through the season, about 15-20 yuan/mu each time. That's the main cost for cotton.

Irrigation 1-2 times, depending on the rain. Picking starts in September, goes through October, multiple rounds. This is the hardest work — that's why I only do 4 mu now. My daughter helps on weekends, and I hire help for 4-5 days at peak.

Last year cotton gave me about 260 kg lint/mu. Price was OK, 6-7 yuan/kg. It's still worth it compared to growing more maize, but barely.
